disagreement_resolutions.resolution: Four distinct accepted raw encodings exist: low-s/high-s each with 27/28 or normalized 0/1 v form. One 20e18 claim paid 80e18.
High. Complete module takeover and full module-held asset loss are demonstrated, including arbitrary execute, but system-wide protocol liquidity or downstream authority is not modeled.

Impact is supported with limitation; severity is Medium. The unauthorized global change is real, but 949e18 debt remained below 1,000e18 contemporaneous collateral value and showed no immediate shortfall.

disagreement_resolutions.reviewer_a: Local denial supported, with permanent-stranding limitation.
disagreement_resolutions.reviewer_b: Supported_with_limitation and prerequisites partially supported because remote semantics are absent.
disagreement_resolutions.resolution: Local denial of an otherwise-valid cross-chain credit is reproduced; permanent source-side stranding, recovery behavior, and deliberate nonce control remain unproven limitations.
Supported_with_limitation. The stale two-dollar feed enabled 1,500e18 debt versus a 750e18 one-dollar pool comparator, while the target lacks an external market-price source.
Medium. Direct duplicate transfer is reproduced, but router B rejects before its own token approval; exploitation needs multiple approved router instances with aligned nonces.

candidates.title: Borrow callback reentrancy finalizes debt after value transfer

root_cause.statement: LendingMarket.borrow transfers stable and invokes an attacker-controlled receiver callback before incrementing the caller's debt, with no reentrancy guard; nested frames therefore validate against stale debt.

required: An ordinary user can deploy a callback receiver and make it the beneficiary of legitimate collateral.
The callback account is healthy for one borrow.
The market has stable liquidity and callback data is nonempty.
prerequisites.limitations: Recursion depth is bounded by available liquidity and gas.

impact.observed: The consensus sample produced 1,500e18 debt and stable against a 750e18 limit. Both reviewers also validated deeper recursion scaling to available market liquidity.
impact.limitations: The attacker must supply legitimate collateral sufficient for one healthy borrow.

scope.rationale: An untrusted protocol-user contract exploits the production borrowing path without trusted-role misconduct or mock-only powers.

final_severity.rationale: One transaction can over-borrow far beyond the collateral limit and scale to draining market stable liquidity, causing immediate insolvency.

candidates.rationale: Positive and negative controls passed in both reviews and the fresh agreement sample.

candidates.title: Bridge credit does not authenticate remote application sender

root_cause.statement: BridgeGateway authenticates the messenger and source chain but never compares messenger.xDomainMessageSender() with remoteGateway[sourceChain]; it reads the sender only for the event.

required: An untrusted remote application can originate a message on a configured source chain.
The trusted messenger honestly relays and reports that mismatching application sender.
The local gateway is the market bridge and the market has stable liquidity.
prerequisites.limitations: No messenger compromise or false source context is required.

impact.observed: A mismatching remote application created 1,000e18 bridge collateral and enabled a 750e18 stable borrow without locked local collateral.
impact.limitations: The unbacked-credit conclusion relies only on the benchmark assumption that remote applications are untrusted.

scope.rationale: Remote applications are explicitly untrusted and the messenger remains honest.

final_severity.rationale: Any untrusted application on a configured source chain can mint arbitrary unbacked collateral credit and drain local market liquidity.

candidates.rationale: Both reviewers reproduced the positive and sender-authentication comparator cases with materially identical conclusions.

candidates.title: Permit relayer can redirect signed transfer

root_cause.statement: recipient controls transferFrom's destination but is absent from TRANSFER_TYPEHASH and the signed payload, so signature validity is invariant under recipient substitution.

required: The owner approved the router for the amount.
A relayer possesses a valid unexpired owner signature for the current token, amount, nonce, and deadline.
The owner intended a fixed recipient.
prerequisites.limitations: Loss cannot exceed the signed amount, available balance, and allowance.

impact.observed: A relayer redirected the full 25e18 signed amount to itself, left the intended recipient at zero, and consumed the owner's nonce.
impact.limitations: A valid signature and token approval are required.

scope.rationale: A permissionless relayer changes security-relevant unsigned calldata in the scoped router.

final_severity.rationale: The omission enables direct theft of the entire authorized transfer amount, subject to a legitimate signature and approval.

candidates.rationale: Both reviewers agreed on reproduction, scope, impact, severity, and distinct remediation.

candidates.title: ECDSA malleability bypasses reward replay protection

root_cause.statement: SignatureCodec accepts low-s/high-s equivalents and 27/28 versus 0/1 v aliases, while RewardsDistributor keys replay state by raw signature bytes instead of claim identity.

required: One legitimate authority-signed claim is available.
The distributor holds enough reward tokens for repeated payouts.
A claimant or relayer can transform public signature values.
prerequisites.limitations: No authority key compromise is needed; the accepted raw-encoding set is finite.

impact.observed: The consensus boundary run accepted four distinct raw encodings for one 20e18 authorization and paid 80e18.
impact.limitations: Amplification is bounded to four accepted raw encodings per authorization under this codec, and by distributor balance.

scope.rationale: The authority remains honest; exploitation uses public signature data and scoped verifier/replay logic.

final_severity.rationale: A legitimate claim can be multiplied fourfold without the signing key, directly overdrawing distributor funds, but exploitation requires a valid authorization and has a finite per-claim multiplier.

candidates.rationale: The consensus boundary execution resolved the reviewers' two-versus-four amplification disagreement in favor of four accepted raw encodings.

candidates.title: StrategyModule can be reinitialized and seized

root_cause.statement: initialize is permissionless, overwrites vault and operator on every call, and never enforces the initialized flag that it sets.

required: A module has been honestly initialized.
The module holds tokens or possesses useful operational authority.
Any untrusted account can submit a transaction.
prerequisites.limitations: Concrete loss depends on assets and downstream authority assigned to the module.

impact.observed: An arbitrary account replaced both roles, drained the full 10e18 module token balance, and independently used the seized vault role for arbitrary execute.
impact.limitations: The frozen target does not connect the module to all protocol liquidity or model downstream privileged integrations.

scope.rationale: An untrusted caller violates the documented vault/operator trust boundary through the production initializer.

final_severity.rationale: Permissionless complete module takeover causes direct loss of all module-held assets and control of its call capability; critical system-wide loss is not demonstrated by the frozen integration.

candidates.rationale: Fresh submitted and consensus boundary runs confirmed role overwrite, sweep, and execute; the deployment-bound impact resolves severity to high.

candidates.title: Any user can raise the global collateral factor

root_cause.statement: The non-guardian branch reverts only when nextFactorBps is less than or equal to the current value, accidentally authorizing any non-guardian increase up to 9,500 bps.

required: The current factor is below 9,500 bps.
An ordinary borrower has collateral.
The market has stable liquidity.
prerequisites.limitations: The hard cap remains 9,500 bps and the guardian can later restore the parameter.

impact.observed: A non-guardian raised the global factor from 7,500 to 9,500 and borrowed 949e18 rather than the former 750e18 limit.
impact.limitations: Fresh boundary execution measured 1,000e18 contemporaneous collateral value versus 949e18 debt: the unauthorized change removes most of the solvency buffer but creates no immediate shortfall at the unchanged fair price.

scope.rationale: A public caller bypasses the documented guardian-only risk-control boundary.

final_severity.rationale: The issue globally weakens a solvency control and enables materially higher leverage, but immediate theft or bad debt is not demonstrated and requires an additional adverse price move or loss mechanism.

candidates.rationale: Fresh reproduction and boundary execution support the access-control defect and limited immediate impact; this resolves the severity disagreement to medium.

candidates.title: Bridge replay nonce is global across source chains

root_cause.statement: processedNonce is keyed only by uint64 nonce even though configured source chains have independent domains, so one chain consumes the same numeric nonce for every chain.

required: At least two source chains are configured.
Their independent message streams use the same numeric nonce.
A valid relay on one source chain executes before the colliding relay.
prerequisites.limitations: The frozen target does not define remote nonce allocation, source escrow, retry, or reissue behavior.

impact.observed: A valid chain-10 nonce-7 relay credited its beneficiary, while an otherwise-valid chain-20 nonce-7 relay reverted and credited zero.
impact.limitations: Local denial of the second credit is demonstrated; permanent source-side collateral stranding and deliberate attacker control of nonce ordering are not.

scope.rationale: The collision occurs in scoped gateway state under honest messenger context.

final_severity.rationale: The flaw can block legitimate cross-chain credits across domains, but proves denial rather than direct theft and lacks remote recovery semantics.

candidates.rationale: The fresh rerun confirms the local denial and comparator while preserving the reviewers' stated remote-system limitation.

candidates.title: Manipulable reserve spot price is trusted during feed fallback

root_cause.statement: On a nonpositive primary answer, ReserveOracle immediately consumes the permissionlessly manipulable current ReservePool ratio without a TWAP, delay, or deviation bound.

required: The honest primary feed is unavailable or returns nonpositive.
The reserve pool and lending market have liquidity.
The attacker can fund a swap material relative to pool depth.
prerequisites.limitations: The feed-failure condition is not attacker-controlled in the reproduction and the attack requires significant temporary capital.

impact.observed: After spending 10,000e18 quote, the attacker manipulated fallback price to about 3.994, borrowed about 14,955e18, and exceeded the one-dollar collateral limit by more than 11,210e18.
impact.limitations: Feasibility depends on feed failure, pool depth, fees, and available lending liquidity.

scope.rationale: Feed failure is an operating condition; swaps, vault deposits, and borrowing are permissionless production paths.

final_severity.rationale: A capitalized ordinary user can create profitable, materially undercollateralized debt during feed failure, with condition and capital requirements keeping it below critical.

candidates.rationale: Both reviewers agreed, and the fresh high-severity agreement sample reproduced the positive and primary-feed negative control.

candidates.title: Positive primary price is accepted indefinitely

root_cause.statement: ReserveOracle ignores updatedAt, roundId, and answeredInRound and accepts every positive answer without a maximum age or round-completeness check.

required: The last positive feed answer becomes stale and materially exceeds current collateral value.
An ordinary borrower has collateral.
The market has stable liquidity.
prerequisites.limitations: The attacker need not and cannot control the configured feed; exploitation is conditional on an honest update outage and price divergence.

impact.observed: A year-old two-dollar answer enabled 1,500e18 debt where the reproduction's contemporaneous one-dollar pool comparator permitted 750e18.
impact.limitations: The target has no external market-price source; the unmanipulated pool ratio is the deterministic current-value comparator.

scope.rationale: Time passing and honest feed outage are system conditions, not trusted-role misconduct.

final_severity.rationale: A stale positive overvaluation can produce immediate, substantial undercollateralized borrowing, though it depends on feed outage and price divergence.

candidates.rationale: The fresh rerun confirms the stale-answer path and freshness-bound comparator; the impact is supported with the shared comparator limitation.

candidates.title: Permit signature replays across router instances

root_cause.statement: The signed payload omits address(this) and block.chainid while each router instance maintains an independent owner nonce, so nonce-aligned instances hash and accept the same signature.

required: The owner approved at least two router instances for the token and amount.
The owner's nonces on those instances are aligned.
A relayer possesses one valid unexpired signature and the owner has sufficient balance.
prerequisites.limitations: Without a second router approval the replay reverts; loss scales only across approved, nonce-aligned instances.

impact.observed: One 25e18 authorization transferred 50e18 across two routers. The boundary run rejected router B before its own approval and accepted the unchanged signature after approval.
impact.limitations: Multiple deployed and approved routers with aligned nonce state are required.

scope.rationale: A permissionless relayer exploits missing verifier-domain separation in the scoped router.

final_severity.rationale: The flaw causes a direct unauthorized extra transfer, but exploitation depends on the significant configuration prerequisite of multiple approved router instances with aligned nonces.

candidates.rationale: Fresh candidate and boundary runs confirmed both the duplicate transfer and the second-approval prerequisite, resolving the severity disagreement to medium.

candidates.title: First-share donation can deny vault deposits

root_cause.statement: With tiny supply and no virtual share/asset offset, a direct underlying donation inflates managed assets so convertToShares floors a comparable victim deposit to zero and deposit reverts.

required: The vault is empty or at a tiny share supply.
The attacker can order a seed and donation before a victim deposit.
The attacker temporarily commits underlying comparable to the blocked deposit.
prerequisites.limitations: Repeated denial requires repeated ordering, gas, and opportunity cost.

impact.observed: The victim deposit reverted and lost no assets; the attacker recovered its 1,000e18 donation plus one-wei seed with zero token loss.
impact.limitations: No victim theft, insolvency, or persistent freeze is shown.

scope.rationale: The attack uses ordinary token transfers, vault deposit/redeem functions, and transaction ordering.

final_severity.rationale: The effect is transient deposit griefing with no victim fund loss, recoverable attacker capital, and a narrow empty/tiny-supply state.

candidates.rationale: Both reviewers and the fresh low-severity agreement sample reproduced the denial and no-donation comparator.

duplicate_analysis.criterion: Candidates cluster only when root cause, impact, and required remediation are all materially identical.

distinctions.reason: Remote-sender authentication and cross-chain nonce namespacing have different causes, impacts, and fixes.
Recipient binding and verifier/chain domain separation have different prerequisites and remediations.
Fallback spot manipulation and primary-feed freshness require independent controls.

isolation_statement.statement: Consensus used only the frozen target/candidate evidence, the two frozen reviewer packages, and files created under consensus-output. No sealed, reveal, ground-truth, Git-history, other-workspace, issue-tracker, network, parent-artifact, rejected-lead, generator, human-assistance, or hidden-truth source was accessed or inferred. Frozen inputs were not modified.
